Apple regularly rolls out new features for Apple Wallet, and upcoming enhancements may revolve around its trade-in programme. Code also suggests Apple could extend the validity period of trade-in quotes from 14 days to 90 days.

Another new feature for Apple Wallet

MacRumors discovered the code referencing this new system within Apple's Guide app. For those unfamiliar, the report notes that Guide is an app "used by Apple employees, Apple Authorised Resellers, and other sales organisations when talking with customers and conducting product demonstrations".

There are multiple strings in the Guide app's code that mention the ability to save trade-in offers to the Wallet app:

  • "You can add this trade-in offer to your Apple Wallet, valid for 90 days."
  • "To save this offer, simply scan the QR code using your iPhone's camera."

The exact implementation of this feature remains unclear. For instance, the code mentions that trade-in offers can be saved for 90 days. Currently, Apple's trade-in quotes are valid for 14 days. Apple may be planning to extend that validity period when it launches this feature.

Today's report also mentions strings within Apple's Guide app referencing a "TradeInKit" framework. According to the report, the new feature is controlled server-side, and the relevant toggle has not yet been activated.

Apple raised trade-in values for most iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch models last week. With prices continuing to rise, trade-in has become an increasingly important part of the Apple shopping experience.
